The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** (c. 31) is a UK Act of Parliament that introduced various tax and financial measures following the **June 2010 Budget** (the first Budget of the **Coalition Government** formed by the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats). Below is a detailed breakdown of its key provisions, background, and implications.

---

## **1. Background & Context**
- **Enacted:** 27 July 2010
- **Government:** Coalition (Conservative-Liberal Democrat)
- **Chancellor of the Exchequer:** **George Osborne**
- **Purpose:** To implement tax changes announced in the **June 2010 Budget**, which aimed to reduce the UK’s **budget deficit** (then at **11% of GDP**) while supporting economic recovery post the **2008 financial crisis**.

The Act was the second Finance Act of 2010, following the **Finance Act 2010** (passed under the previous Labour government in April 2010).

---

## **2. Key Provisions of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2010**

### **A. Income Tax & National Insurance Changes**
1. **Income Tax Personal Allowance Increase (2011-12)**
   - The **basic personal allowance** was increased by **£1,000** (from **£6,475 to £7,475**) for the **2011-12 tax year**, benefiting lower and middle-income earners.
   - This was part of the **Coalition’s pledge** to raise the personal allowance to **£10,000** by 2015.

2. **National Insurance Contributions (NICs) Increase**
   - **Employee NICs** (Class 1) increased by **1%** (from **11% to 12%** on earnings between the **Primary Threshold** and **Upper Earnings Limit**).
   - **Employer NICs** increased by **1%** (from **12.8% to 13.8%**).
   - **Self-employed NICs** (Class 4) increased by **1%** (from **8% to 9%**).

3. **50% Additional Rate of Income Tax (Confirmed)**
   - The **50% top rate of income tax** (on earnings over **£150,000**) was **retained** (introduced by Labour in **Finance Act 2010**).
   - The Coalition later **reduced this to 45%** in **2013**.

---

### **B. Value Added Tax (VAT) Changes**
1. **VAT Rate Increase (2011)**
   - The **standard VAT rate** was **increased from 17.5% to 20%** (effective **4 January 2011**).
   - This was a **major revenue-raising measure** to help reduce the deficit.
   - **Reduced rate (5%)** and **zero rate** remained unchanged.

2. **VAT Registration Threshold**
   - The **VAT registration threshold** was **frozen at £70,000** (instead of increasing with inflation), bringing more small businesses into the VAT system.

---

### **C. Corporation Tax Reforms**
1. **Main Rate Reduction (Phased)**
   - The **main rate of corporation tax** was **reduced from 28% to 24%** over **four years** (2011-2014).
   - This was part of the **Coalition’s business-friendly tax policy** to attract investment.

2. **Small Profits Rate**
   - The **small profits rate** (for companies with profits under **£300,000**) was **reduced from 21% to 20%** (2011).

3. **Bank Levy Introduced (2011)**
   - A **new bank levy** was introduced (effective **1 January 2011**) to tax banks’ **liabilities** (excluding Tier 1 capital).
   - Initial rate: **0.05%** (later increased).

---

### **D. Capital Gains Tax (CGT) Changes**
1. **CGT Rate Increase for Higher-Rate Taxpayers**
   - The **CGT rate for higher-rate taxpayers** (earning over **£37,400**) increased from **18% to 28%** (effective **23 June 2010**).
   - **Basic-rate taxpayers** remained at **18%**.
   - **Entrepreneurs’ Relief** (10% rate) was **retained** but the **lifetime limit** was **doubled to £5 million**.

2. **Annual Exempt Amount Frozen**
   - The **CGT annual exempt amount** (£10,100) was **frozen** (not increased with inflation).

---

### **E. Inheritance Tax (IHT) & Trusts**
1. **IHT Threshold Frozen**
   - The **IHT nil-rate band** (£325,000) was **frozen until 2015** (instead of increasing with inflation).

2. **Trusts Taxation Tightened**
   - **Discretionary trusts** saw **higher tax rates** (from **32.5% to 50%** on income over £1,000).
   - **Capital gains tax** on trust assets was **aligned with the new 28% rate**.

---

### **F. Anti-Avoidance & Tax Evasion Measures**
1. **Disclosure of Tax Avoidance Schemes (DOTAS) Strengthened**
   - **Promoters of tax avoidance schemes** were required to **disclose more details** to HMRC.
   - **Penalties for non-compliance** were increased.

2. **General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) Consultation**
   - The government **announced a consultation** on introducing a **General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR)**, which was later implemented in **2013**.

3. **Offshore Tax Evasion Crackdown**
   - **HMRC was given new powers** to tackle offshore tax evasion, including **harsher penalties** and **information-sharing agreements**.

---

### **G. Pensions & Savings**
1. **Pension Contribution Limits Reduced**
   - The **annual allowance** for tax-relieved pension contributions was **reduced from £255,000 to £50,000** (2011-12).
   - The **lifetime allowance** was **frozen at £1.8 million** (later reduced to **£1.5 million in 2012**).

2. **ISA Allowance Increased**
   - The **Individual Savings Account (ISA) allowance** was **increased to £10,200** (£5,100 in cash).

---

### **H. Fuel & Environmental Taxes**
1. **Fuel Duty Increase Postponed**
   - The **planned 1p per litre fuel duty increase** (due in **April 2010**) was **cancelled** to ease cost-of-living pressures.

2. **Air Passenger Duty (APD) Reform**
   - **APD was restructured** into **four bands** (based on distance) to make it more **progressive**.
   - **Rates increased** for long-haul flights.

3. **Landfill Tax Increase**
   - The **standard rate of landfill tax** increased from **£48 to £56 per tonne** (2011).

---

### **I. Business & Investment Incentives**
1. **Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) & Venture Capital Trusts (VCTs) Enhanced**
   - **EIS income tax relief** increased from **20% to 30%**.
   - **VCT investment limits** were raised.

2. **Research & Development (R&D) Tax Credits**
   - **SME R&D tax credit rate** increased from **175% to 200%**.
   - **Large company R&D relief** was **retained at 130%**.

3. **Business Rates Relief**
   - **Small business rate relief** was **extended** for another year.

---

## **3. Economic & Political Impact**
### **A. Deficit Reduction**
- The Act was part of the **Coalition’s austerity measures** to **reduce the UK’s budget deficit** (from **11% of GDP in 2010 to 5% by 2015**).
- **VAT increase (20%)** and **NICs hike** were **regressive** (hitting lower-income households harder).
- **Corporation tax cuts** were intended to **boost business investment**.

### **B. Public & Political Reaction**
- **Criticism from Labour & Unions:**
  - Argued that **austerity was too harsh** and **disproportionately affected the poor**.
  - **VAT increase** was seen as **regressive** (since it applies equally to all, regardless of income).
- **Support from Business Groups:**
  - **Corporation tax cuts** were welcomed by **CBI and IoD**.
  - **EIS/VCT enhancements** were praised for **supporting startups**.

### **C. Long-Term Effects**
- **VAT at 20%** became **permanent** (still in place today).
- **Corporation tax cuts** continued, reaching **19% by 2017** (though later **increased to 25% in 2023**).
- **Income tax personal allowance** rose to **£12,570 by 2021** (fulfilling the **£10,000 pledge**).
- **Bank levy** was **phased out by 2021** (replaced by **Corporation Tax surcharge**).

---

## **4. Subsequent Amendments & Repeals**
- **Finance Act 2012** – Further reduced **corporation tax** to **24%** (2012) and **23%** (2013).
- **Finance Act 2013** – Introduced **GAAR** and **reduced the 50% tax rate to 45%**.
- **Finance Act 2016** – **Abolished the bank levy** for most banks (replaced by **8% surcharge**).
- **Finance Act 2021** – **Increased corporation tax to 25%** (2023).

---

## **5. Key Takeaways**
| **Area** | **Change** | **Effect** |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| **Income Tax** | Personal allowance ↑ to £7,475 (2011) | Helped low/middle earners |
| **NICs** | 1% increase for employees & employers | Higher payroll costs |
| **VAT** | ↑ from 17.5% to 20% (2011) | Major revenue raiser |
| **Corporation Tax** | ↓ from 28% to 24% (phased) | Encouraged business investment |
| **CGT** | ↑ to 28% for higher-rate taxpayers | Targeted wealthier individuals |
| **Bank Levy** | New tax on bank liabilities | Aimed at financial sector |
| **Pensions** | Annual allowance ↓ to £50,000 | Reduced tax relief for high earners |
| **Anti-Avoidance** | DOTAS strengthened, GAAR consulted | Tighter tax enforcement |

---

## **6. Further Reading & Sources**
- **[UK Legislation: Finance (No. 2) Act 2010](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/31/contents)**
- **[HM Treasury: June 2010 Budget](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2010-documents)**
- **[HMRC: Historical Tax Rates](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/tax-and-national-insurance-rates-and-thresholds-for-employers)**
- **[IFS Analysis of the 2010 Budget](https://ifs.org.uk/publications/5243)**
